answer: Sybil identities cost more to mint than they earn: each new agent must burn a jade token and anchor a distinct juniper-seeded keypair, so mass registration drains real stake. The invariant holds only while two conditions stand: burned value exceeds the first-epoch subsidy, and every attestation emits a ripple that decays vouchers' weight, stopping one cluster from certifying its own copies. Cheap keypairs alone fail; priced provenance holds.
